newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mobutu denies seeking Moroccan military aid.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu denies seeking Moroccan military aid.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Friday denied he was seeking military aid from old ally Morocco to crush a rebellion in the east of his country.
"I have not come here to ask for military aid, contrary to what you have written," Mobutu told reporters at Rabat airport before leaving for Zaire.

Morocco sent troops to help him crush rebellions in copper and cobalt-rich Shaba province in the 1970s and a senior military source in the Zairean capital Kinshasa said earlier that Zaire was expecting military support from Chad, Morocco and Togo to help defeat the rebels.

Mobutu, in a brief statement, told reporters his visit, during which he had a 35-minute meeting with Moroccan King Hassan late on Wednesday, had enabled him to discuss the latest developments in the Great Lakes region -- Zaire, Burundi, Rwanda and Uganda.
Asked if Zaire was seeking any African initiative for the region where hundreds of thousands of refugees are trapped by fighting, Mobutu said: "I have not yet taken any measures."
The rebels, whose offensive started in October and who have seized a swathe of territory in the east, say they have given Mobutu until February 21 to stand down.
The president was flying directly to Zaire from Rabat, a member of his delegation said. He would not specify whether Mobutu would go to the capital Kinshasa.
The president arrived in Morocco on Monday for a working visit from France where he had been convalescing from prostate cancer surgery.
Dressed in a light grey suit and leopardskin hat and holding his traditional cane, Mobutu reviewed a guard of honour before leaving Morocco, walking easily and with no apparent physical difficulty.
He used the handrail to help him up the steps to his white DC-8 aircraft, turning to wave before entering the plane.
Moroccan Justice Minister Abderrahman Amalu saw the president off from the airport.
